note: Two unrelated groups whose engine codes do not collide. Rover's range was half its own K-series petrol and half bought-in: Honda petrol fours in the 200/400/600, its own L-series 2.0 diesel, and a PSA XUD. The L-series and the XUD were both recorded as petrol. Chrysler, Dodge and Plymouth share one engine-code scheme, nearly all of it petrol; the exception is the VM Motori 2.5 turbo-diesel, which Dodge and Plymouth recorded as petrol while Chrysler had it right. Capacities are family figures unless stated otherwise.

engines.source: Rover's own L-series 2.0 diesel (20 T2N, 20 T2R, 20 T4G, 20 T4H) in the 200, 400, 600 and 25/45, and the PSA XUD 7TE in the earlier cars. Both recorded as petrol. Pre-common-rail with no particulate filter, so a conventional 10W-40 is correct.

Rover K-series petrol (11 K2D, 14 K2A/K2D/K2F/K4F, 16 K4F, 18 K4F/K4K, 25 K4F) - Metro, 200, 25, 45, MGF. The head-gasket reputation of this engine makes the correct grade and a disciplined change interval worth respecting.
The Honda petrol fours Rover fitted to the 200, 400 and 600 under licence (D 16 A8, D 16 Y2, D 16 Z2, D16B2, F 18 A3, F 20 Z1, F 20 Z2, H 23 A3). Same figures the Honda table gives them.
The VM Motori 2.5 turbo-diesel in the Voyager and Cherokee. Chrysler had it recorded as diesel and Dodge and Plymouth as petrol - the same engine, three different answers.
Chrysler and Dodge V8 and V10 (5.2, 5.9 and 8.0) - Ram, Durango, Viper. Large sump.
Chrysler, Dodge and Plymouth V6 (2.5 to 3.9) - Voyager, Neon, Stratus, Sebring, Cherokee.
Chrysler, Dodge and Plymouth four-cylinder petrol (1.8 to 2.5) - Neon, Stratus, PT Cruiser, Voyager.
